onboardingPhaseGoogleTakeoutDescription: Go to https://takeout.google.com/ and select your favorite albums for export (make sure to include the "Albums" and "Photos" data).
onboardingPhaseConfigureFoldersDescripti: Once you have your Google Takeout data, extract the downloaded archive to a folder on your computer. Point the application to the folder containing your Google Takeout data.
onboardingPhaseIndexDescription: Explore your photos in different ways: view them by albums, see them on a globe based on where they were taken, or check the indexing status of your albums. Click on any album or photo to see more details and relive your memories!
onboardingWelcomeBody: Welcome to TravelAlbums! Visualize and explore your photo collection of your travels. To get started, follow the steps in this onboarding process to import your photos and discover new ways to relive your memories.
onboardingWelcomeSubtitle: In the next steps, you'll learn how to export your photos from Google Photos using Google Takeout, configure the application to access your photo library, and explore the various features that TravelAlbums has to offer. Let's get started on this exciting journey to rediscover your memories!
onboardingWelcomeFooter: Thanks for using TravelAlbums, and we hope you enjoy exploring your photo collection in a whole new way!

releasePageIntro: Welcome to the Trip Gallery release page - a compact tour of features, architecture and core concepts. Enjoy the highlights and feel free to explore the codebase for details! ✨
releaseHighlightsItem3: Rich browsing: map/globe, search, filters, and date grouping 🗺️🔎
releaseHighlightsItem4: State organized via lightweight context stores and custom hooks 🧠
releaseHighlightsItem5: Developer-friendly scripts for ingesting Takeout exports and more 📦
releaseFeaturesItem1: Generate thumbnails & metadata from Takeout or folders (scripts/) 🛠️
releaseFeaturesItem2: Efficient client-side photo indexing and metrics (indexer) 📊
releaseFeaturesItem3: Favorites, pinned and private photo collections ⭐📌🔒
releaseFeaturesItem4: Geolocation-aware views using airports & capitals data ✈️🏙️
releaseFeaturesItem5: Accessible UI helpers: theme switcher, tools, drawers, and modals 🎛️
releaseFrontendBody: Vite + React + TypeScript - fast HMR and modern DX. UI is componentized under src/components.
releaseStateBody: application state lives in Context stores (src/context) and reusable hooks (src/hooks) to keep logic decoupled from UI.
releaseServerBody: lightweight Node utilities and scripts live in server-utils/ and scripts/ for thumbnailing, metadata extraction, and takeout conversion - these are intended to be run as offline/preprocess steps.
releaseDataBody: photos are indexed with normalized metadata (dates, GPS, albums, tags). The indexer computes metrics for efficient filtering and grouped views.
releaseUxBody: single-component pages, modular tools/drawers, and small focused components for predictable composition and easy testing.
releaseConceptsItem1: Ingest photos and metadata using the provided scripts (Takeout helpers, thumbnail generators). The preprocess step creates thumbnails and structured metadata files.
releaseConceptsItem2: The client reads the metadata and hydrates context stores for search, filters, and UI state. Components subscribe to stores via hooks like useAllPhotos.
releaseConceptsItem3: UI components render grouped/photo grid views, map views, and interactive drawers for details - all driven by the centralized stores and small, testable hooks.
releaseDeveloperNotesItem1: Explore scripts/ for batch tools and server-utils/ for helpers.
releaseDeveloperNotesItem2: Look in src/context for the canonical app state and derived selectors.
releaseDeveloperNotesItem3: Custom hooks live in src/hooks and should be preferred for reusable logic.
